digest.component_or_area: code-review impact model and tests criterion
propositions: The code-v3 impact model discards verifier user-reach judgments (prod_impact and trigger_likelihood), causing test findings to score ~0.30 in the maintainability lane and remain advisory despite load-bearing consequences.

A contract-contradicting-assertion antipattern (test forbidding a state the same diff's contract declares allowed) is not detected in Pass-1 recall, allowing such contradictions to ship through review.

The maintainability lane's churn-based dampener penalizes findings lacking churn90 data as ×0.5, compressing scores regardless of prod_impact; the 70 prod=medium/high test findings are uniformly consequential but starved.
The reversibility floor is lane-blind and can lift a minor debt binary on a hard_to_reverse surface to 0.6, crossing the tests@0.54 threshold when tests findings should not block.

The code-v4 impact model must split maintainability by consequence class (serious undamped; moderate prod_impact-keyed; debt churn-amplified only), restrict reversibility floor to consequence lanes, and introduce forbids_contract_allowed_state with both-halves-verbatim evidence.

The tests criterion must transition from advisory@0.95 to blocking@0.54, routing pins, and version references must update from code-v3 to code-v4 without rewriting or re-scoring existing stored sidecars.
